_about: The Agentic Site Framework as data. asf.py reads this to check gates and say what's next; the /asf command reads it to run a stage. Paths are relative to the client project root. Check types are documented in orchestrator/README.md.

roles.lead: Owns the client relationship and signs every gate (a PM, strategist or account owner)
roles.designer: Reviews the design on the review page and the built pages; doesn't push pixels
roles.developer: Theme, plugin, deployment, hosting and access
roles.content: Copy, page briefs and the facts behind them
roles.qa: Runs the checks no script can and reads every page as the buyer
roles.client: The client's own approver: confirms facts, chooses the message and the design, signs off staging

change._about: After launch, every piece of work is a change (bin/asf change): one issue, one branch, one pull request, and the gates below that fit its kind. Each gate has a signer role; items owned by another role need that person's confirmation first. A check or item with "kinds" applies only to those kinds. {change.file} and {change.slug} are filled in.

kind_help.fix: Something broken: a link, a form, a layout bug
kind_help.content: New or changed copy on a page that exists
kind_help.page: A new page or a new section
kind_help.design: A restyle with the same words
kind_help.rework: A new service line, a rebrand or a new site structure: strategy and IA change first

gates.title: Brief
gates.question: What are we changing, and why?
gates.why: Ten minutes agreeing what and why saves building the wrong thing, and names the number that will say whether it worked.

checks.label: The request it answers is linked
checks.hint: `bin/asf change set {change.slug} issue <number or link>` (file the request first: /asf intake)

checks.label: The pages it touches are named
checks.hint: `bin/asf change set {change.slug} pages /pricing/,/services/`

checks.label: What and why is written
checks.hint: Fill “What and why” in {change.file}, in the client's words where there are any

checks.label: What it should move is named (the weekly report follows it up)
checks.hint: Fill “What it should move” in {change.file}: one number, where it stands today, and when to look

checks.label: The page's sections are planned
checks.hint: Fill the Sections table in {change.file} (docs/framework/patterns/page-recipes.md)

checks.label: 8 sections at most
checks.hint: Cut or merge sections: one idea, one home

manual: The request is the client's own, with its source on the issue

manual.text: Every new fact, number or name is in docs/truth.md as public, or marked [CONFIRM] for the client
docs/01-strategy.md and docs/02-information-architecture.md are updated for this change, and the client agreed to them

gates.title: Design
gates.question: How does it look?
gates.why: The designer sees it before the client does, and before it's built everywhere. It's also where anything that can't be built as drawn is said out loud.

checks.label: Shared with the designer for review (a Claude artifact)
checks.hint: Put the changed pages on a review page at 1440 and 375 and publish it as a Claude artifact (docs/framework/prompts/07-design-direction.md C), then `bin/asf change set {change.slug} review <link>`

checks.label: No feedback on this change is left open
checks.hint: `bin/asf feedback list`, then `bin/asf feedback close <id> --outcome applied|declined|overruled --note …`

manual: Reviewed on the review page at 1440 and 375; every comment is resolved or filed as a type:design issue
Uses the site's own tokens and components, and passes the anti-AI-look checklist
The review is recorded (`bin/asf feedback add`), and a comment that should hold from now on is a rule in docs/lessons.md

manual.text: Everything shown can be built with the tools the brief names; anything that can't is listed

gates.title: Build
gates.question: Is it right?
gates.why: Scripts catch what people miss, and people catch what scripts miss. Merging before both means fixing it on the live site.

checks.label: Content lint: no errors
checks.hint: Run the lint and fix what it lists

checks.label: Its pages have no [CONFIRM] chips left
checks.hint: Get each fact confirmed (or cut the claim), add it to docs/truth.md, remove the chip

checks.label: Its pages load, with no accessibility or performance errors (staging, or the local site)
checks.hint: `python3 docs/framework/qa/launch.py <site> --pages <its pages> --only accessibility,performance` shows what's wrong

checks.label: A pull request is open and closes the issue
checks.hint: Open it with “Closes #<issue>”, then `bin/asf change set {change.slug} pr <link>`

checks.label: No feedback on this change is left open
checks.hint: `bin/asf feedback list`, then `bin/asf feedback close <id> --outcome applied|declined|overruled --note …`

manual: Opens in the block editor with no invalid blocks, and its forms and links work

manual.text: Reads right as the buyer: one idea, one home, nothing repeated from another page
The code was reviewed on the pull request

gates.title: Release
gates.question: Is it live, and safe?
gates.why: Live is not the same as staging: caches, plugins and data differ. Someone looks at production, and the client hears that it's done.

checks.label: Released to production (date recorded)
checks.hint: Merge, deploy (docs/07-deployment.md), then `bin/asf change set {change.slug} released <date>`

checks.label: Its pages are live on production, with no accessibility or performance errors
checks.hint: Check the deploy and the cache; `python3 docs/framework/qa/launch.py <production> --pages <its pages> --only accessibility,performance`

manual.text: Checked on production itself, not only on staging
The client signed off the change, on its review issue or on staging

manual: The issue is closed, and the client knows it's live

stages.title: Truth
stages.question: What is true about this business, and what can we prove in public?
stages.why: A site built on claims nobody checked gets rewritten after the client reads it, or after a customer does.

checks.label: Goal document filled (no [brackets] left)
checks.hint: Fill it from the kickoff call; templates/goal-document.md

checks.label: Current-site audit done
checks.hint: Prompt 01 with the site-researcher agent. No current site? `asf skip G1 audit --reason "no site"`

checks.label: Business arc written in the client's words
checks.hint: Prompt 02 (truth harvest) with the site-researcher agent

checks.label: At least 5 claims, each with a source and status
checks.hint: Prompt 02; every number, name and quote gets a row

checks.label: At least 10 verbatim lines in the voice bank
checks.hint: Quote the founders and their customers; never paraphrase

checks.label: Every image in content/media/ is in the truth file's image map
checks.hint: Open each image and record what it really shows (truth.md §6)

checks.label: Competitor and reference teardown done
checks.hint: Prompt 03 with the site-researcher agent

checks.label: Every raw source in docs/intake/raw/ read and filed
checks.hint: /asf intake: one item per request (GitHub issue or docs/intake/items/), then `asf intake done <file>`

manual: The client signed the goal document
The founder agrees with the business arc
Constraints (white-label, names that can’t appear, regulated claims) are written down, and those names are in docs/framework/qa/config.json → "forbidden"

stages.title: Story
stages.question: What do we say, to whom, in what order, on which page?
stages.why: Design and copy both follow the message. If the message is wrong, every page built on it is redone.

checks.label: Strategy written (no [brackets] left)
checks.hint: Prompt 04 with the site-strategist agent

checks.label: The client's own words choosing the message are recorded
checks.hint: Ask which route defines their business; quote the answer

checks.label: Information architecture done
checks.hint: Prompt 05 with the site-strategist agent

checks.label: Page briefs written (at least 3)
checks.hint: Prompt 05; one brief per page from templates/page-brief.md

checks.label: Every brief has 8 sections or fewer
checks.hint: One idea, one home: link instead of repeating

manual: The client chose a messaging route and said it defines their business
The defining line fails the competitor test

manual.text: Every recurring idea has exactly one home page

stages.title: System
stages.question: How does it look, and how does it work?
stages.why: The client and the designer see the real pages before every page is built in that look. Changing direction afterwards is ten times the work.

checks.label: Client facts file filled (entity.php)
checks.hint: Fill inc/entity.php from the truth file first

checks.label: Design brief written from the raw data
checks.hint: Prompt 07: geography, buyer, category codes, price, their own world

checks.label: Three design directions compared
checks.hint: Prompt 07; the client chooses

checks.label: Directions shared for review (a Claude artifact for the team)
checks.hint: Stage 3.2a: preview each direction (/?asf_direction=a), publish them on one review page as a Claude artifact, then `asf set design.review_url https://…`

checks.label: The client chose a direction
checks.hint: Record the client's choice: `asf set design.direction "B, chosen by <name> on <date>"`

checks.label: No design feedback is left open
checks.hint: `bin/asf feedback list`, then `bin/asf feedback close <id> --outcome applied|declined|overruled --note …`; promote what should hold from now on

checks.label: The client's own design layer is in place
checks.hint: Write the chosen design into assets/css/brand.css + theme.json

checks.label: Every page in the IA exists in content/, and no skeleton page is left that the IA doesn't plan
checks.hint: Write the missing pages (prompt 06); rename or delete skeleton pages the IA doesn't list (then bin/setup.sh --reseed)

checks.label: Content lint: no errors
checks.hint: Fix what lint_content.py reports

manual.text: Every review comment, on the review page and on the client's review issue, is resolved or filed as a type:design issue
Designer review passes the anti-AI-look checklist
Not a re-skin: palette, type, layout and components differ from the wireframe and from other clients

manual: The client approved the home page and one inner page in the browser

stages.title: Ship
stages.question: Is it right, secure, fast, accessible, finished and deployed?
stages.why: Launch is the one moment the whole site is checked at once. What slips through here is found by visitors.

checks.label: Every raw source in docs/intake/raw/ read and filed (nothing the client sent is left unread at launch)
checks.hint: /asf intake: one item per request (GitHub issue or docs/intake/items/), then `asf intake done <file>`

checks.label: Strict lint: no errors and no [CONFIRM] chips left
checks.hint: Get every [CONFIRM] answered by the client, or remove the claim

checks.label: Crawl: no errors, and no [CONFIRM] left on any page, title or meta description
checks.hint: Fix what crawl.py reports; pages left over from the skeleton are removed with bin/setup.sh --reseed or in WordPress

checks.label: Deployed to staging
checks.hint: Deploy (docs/07-deployment.md), then `asf set deploy.staging_url https://…`

checks.label: Accessibility scan: no errors (alt text, names, labels, language, zoom)
checks.hint: Fix what launch.py reports; then run qa/contrast.js in the browser for colour contrast

checks.label: Security scan on staging: no errors (HTTPS, headers, exposed files, login-name leaks)
checks.hint: Fix what launch.py reports; set ASF_WP_USER and ASF_WP_APP_PASSWORD to include pending updates and risky settings

checks.label: Performance budget on staging: no errors (response time, compression, page weight, images)
checks.hint: Resize and compress images first; then caching and compression at the host

checks.label: Launch settings on staging: robots, sitemap, real 404s, privacy link, no local URLs, forms and email
checks.hint: Fix what launch.py reports

checks.label: Lighthouse (mobile) 90+ on home and two inner pages
checks.hint: Needs a public staging URL (it's sent to Google PageSpeed Insights). Behind a password? Run Lighthouse in Chrome DevTools, then `bin/asf skip G4 lighthouse --reason "scores …"`

manual.text: Colour contrast passes (qa/contrast.js) in every colour context, and a keyboard-only pass reaches the menu, every link and the form
Block editor shows zero invalid blocks
The enquiry form works end to end on staging, and the email arrives (not in spam)
Backups run daily at the host, are kept at least 30 days, and one restore has been tested
Uptime monitoring on the production URL alerts a named person
Every admin has a personal login, a strong password and two-factor authentication

manual: The client signed off staging in writing

stages.title: Run
stages.question: Is the site doing its job, and what do we change next?
stages.why: A site nobody measures drifts: a plugin update, an expired certificate or a dead form goes unnoticed for weeks.

checks.label: Live in production
checks.hint: `bin/asf set deploy.production_url https://…`

checks.label: Production scan: no security or launch errors (rechecked weekly)
checks.hint: Fix what launch.py reports: a plugin update, a host change or an expiring certificate can undo launch work

checks.label: Live campaigns pass their checks; finished ones are closed
checks.hint: `bin/asf campaign check <slug>` shows what's wrong; close finished ones with `bin/asf campaign close <slug> --outcome keep|redirect|unpublish`

checks.label: No change is stuck: none idle for two weeks, none built but unreleased for a week
checks.hint: `bin/asf change list` shows each open change and who it waits on; move it on, or `bin/asf change drop <slug> --reason …`

checks.label: Feedback has been looked at for rules in the last five weeks
checks.hint: /asf learn: `bin/asf feedback patterns`, promote what should hold, then `bin/asf feedback reviewed --by "Name"`

checks.label: Analytics tag live on the production site
checks.hint: Set ASF_GA4_ID (or ASF_GTM_ID) in production's wp-config, then `bin/asf set measurement.analytics "GA4 G-XXXX"`; the check looks for that ID on the live home page

checks.label: AI-search prompts to track are listed
checks.hint: `bin/asf set measurement.prompts '["best … for …", "…"]'` (5 prompts buyers would ask)

checks.label: This week's numbers collected
checks.hint: `bin/asf report` (or /asf report)

checks.label: This week's report written (no [blanks] left)
checks.hint: /asf report: the agent writes "The three things" from the data; you review it

manual: This week's report was reviewed and sent to the client
It names one concrete action for the coming week, with an owner
